summary: The pack is structurally valid and provides accurate media metadata, verbatim SRT cues, shot representatives, cue representatives, and a 1.5-second dense frame probe. It is sufficient to recover the tutorial's coarse sequence, but it contains no OCR, no semantic observations, and no claim-level provenance. Two material SRT recognition errors are preserved as if they were ground truth. Critical details such as the Kimi refinement turns, JiMeng settings/candidate state, editing-project state, result-shot contents, character drift, and all authorization/export/publication unknowns are not encoded semantically.

contracts.note: Verbatim preservation is only relative to the supplied SRT; it does not make the SRT transcription accurate against the audiovisual source.

groundTruthChecks.evidencePackAssessment: Recoverable from cues plus frames, but not represented as semantic stages. SHOT-017 and SHOT-018 divide the handoff/result boundary more precisely than the subtitle cue alone.

groundTruth: Initial prompt asks for an approximately 30-second healing solo-woman Vlog storyboard with opening/middle/ending and per-shot AI image prompts.
A follow-up says the storyboard lacks empty shots, is all people, and asks for five room/interior/furniture/decor empty shots.
A further correction says room empty shots must anticipate future advertiser product placement and cites air purifiers and robot vacuums as suitable examples.
The interface visibly shows Kimi and an '已阅读55个网页' state during the later response.
groundTruthChecks.evidencePackAssessment: The frame assets can prove multiple turns, but the JSON contains neither OCR nor a turn-level description; transcript-only reconstruction would incorrectly collapse this into a single prompt/response.

groundTruthChecks.evidencePackAssessment: Visually present but absent as structured evidence. Do not infer an exact number of prompts or final selected scene assets solely from 16/16.

groundTruth: A desktop nonlinear-editing timeline is shown with multiple vertical still-image clips on the primary track.
Several short blue audio clips are placed on lower tracks for ambience/effects; the narration names outdoor birds and running/brushing water as examples.
A long music waveform is added on a lower track and a visible level readout shows -1.8 dB in one frame.
The editor preview cycles through a woman/cat scene, an air-purifier room, a reading scene, and a robot-vacuum scene.
The visible project time display is around 00:00:51:17 with total 00:02:36:03; this is editor-project state, not proof that the tutorial's result excerpt or exported deliverable is 2:36.
groundTruthChecks.evidencePackAssessment: The timeline is visible, but the JSON does not identify the editor, clip inventory, track layout, asset names, effects, transition types, music title, or exact project settings. Presence of claimed motion/transitions is only partially demonstrable.

groundTruthChecks.evidencePackAssessment: Shot boundaries and representatives capture the six-image result sequence well, but the JSON provides no semantic shot descriptions.

groundTruthChecks.groundTruth: The tutorial claims that selecting reference-character features/style can keep images consistent. The final excerpt does not demonstrate strict identity consistency: the daytime reading woman has long black hair and one facial/outfit design, while the night candle woman has a short bob, different face proportions, and a different outfit. Earlier generated candidates also vary in hair length, clothing, and rendering details.
groundTruthChecks.evidencePackAssessment: No identity-consistency metric or cross-shot comparison is present. The pack should not upgrade the narrator's method claim into an observed successful result.

groundTruthChecks.groundTruth: The Kimi revision explicitly optimizes empty shots for future ad insertion, and generated/result images visibly stage air purifiers and a robot vacuum. These are mock/generated placements; visible labels are synthetic or illegible and do not establish a real brand, sponsor, paid collaboration, product claim, or approval.
groundTruthChecks.evidencePackAssessment: Product-placement intent is recoverable from audio and frames, but commercial status must remain unknown.

groundTruthChecks.groundTruth: The presenter instructs viewers to find a reference image to copy/transform for the desired style. The video does not identify the reference source, creator, license, permission, model/likeness consent, or the usage terms of Kimi/JiMeng assets. Kimi's visible reading of 55 webpages also does not provide source-level attribution in the tutorial.
groundTruthChecks.evidencePackAssessment: No authorization or provenance records exist in the pack.

groundTruthChecks.groundTruth: The video shows an editor project and an in-video result preview, but no export dialog, export path, output codec/bitrate, completed render receipt, upload flow, publication URL, account-post record, or platform analytics for this generated Vlog.
groundTruthChecks.evidencePackAssessment: The source MP4's own encoding metadata must not be confused with export proof for the demonstrated Vlog.
